propositions: Subagents spawn CPU saturation workers (python -c 'while True: pass') to reproduce timing-dependent failures but fail to reap them, causing orphans to be reparented to PID 1 and run indefinitely.

38 CPU-saturation processes orphaned on 2026-08-22 ran for four days at ~1341% combined CPU, consuming 138,000 total CPU-seconds and driving load average to 58.49, making applications unlaunchable until manual pkill.

Agent guidance lacks binding requirements that background load generators be time-bounded at spawn (e.g. via timeout) and that subagents reap child processes before returning, including on error paths.

A detection mechanism is needed to identify compute processes orphaned to PID 1 with high accumulated CPU time (threshold 3600 CPU-seconds by default) so leaked batches can be found and operators notified.
